basics.name: Xingtian (James) Si
basics.summary: M.A. Economics student at the University of Chicago. Researcher in causal inference and causal machine learning, with a focus on consumer behavior, targeting, and policy evaluation.

work.organization: UC San Diego, Rady School of Management (RA for Prof. Sally Sadoff)
work.position: Research Assistant — Correspondence Audit Studies on Labor Market Discrimination
highlights: Systematically reviewed 22 correspondence audit studies; constructed and audited a 53-sheet database of 600+ fictitious names.
Harmonized eight name-perception studies into a dataset of 1,600+ names and 25 variables.
Processed data from 10,000+ respondents and 44,000+ observations in Python.

work.position: When Does Plug-in Data Thinning Work? Validity Boundaries, Misspecification and Choose-then-Infer in Econometric Panels
highlights: Derived an asymptotic characterization of dependence induced by plug-in covariance estimation in clustered panels.
Established sufficient conditions for asymptotically valid post-selection inference based on fixed-dimensional linear aggregates.
Conducted Monte Carlo experiments (DiD, event-study pretesting, covariate screening) and a county-level minimum-wage placebo application.

work.organization: University of Nottingham Ningbo China (supervised by Assoc. Prof. Haibo Xu)
work.position: Co-authored Research — When Click-to-Cancel Creates Complexity: A Theory of Subscription Regulation
highlights: Developed a theoretical model of joint cancellation-friction and retention-menu complexity choice; derived a substitution mechanism.
Showed the consumer-welfare-maximizing friction cap can be interior; extended the model to friction-induced fatigue and joint regulation.

work.organization: University of Nottingham Ningbo China (supervised by Assoc. Prof. Zhenjiang Lin)
work.position: Dissertation — Causal Machine Learning and Counterfactual Inference in Consumer Behavior
highlights: 12,007 scenario-survey responses across 490 demographic profiles; cross-fitted IPW estimates an 18.3 pp reduction in stated acceptance.
Separated heterogeneity discovery from confirmation via profile-cluster sample splitting (causal forests, T-learners).
Effect-based targeting showed 29–42% lower acceptance losses than random allocation.

work.organization: Columbia University (RA for Dr. Jiaxi Yang)
work.position: Research Assistant — Early Childhood Intervention and Mathematics Achievement
highlights: Analyzed baseline differences between special-education and general-education cohorts across six domains.
Applied causal random forests to heterogeneous effects of special-education services on fifth-grade math achievement.
Developed interactive dashboards in R Shiny and Python Dash.

work.organization: University of Nottingham (supervised by Prof. Abigail Barr)
work.position: Team Member — Do Female Directors Improve the Financial Performance of Companies
highlights: Econometric analysis of 840 UK firm-year observations (2008–2016) using Stata (ROA and Tobin's Q).
Found an inverted-U relationship between female board representation and Tobin's Q, turning point around 20–25%.
